extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal counsel for education institutions, policy implementers, and other recipients of Federal funding
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for recipients' Title IX grievance procedures, including evidentiary exclusions (rape-shield), notice requirements, dismissal rules, and how recipients may tailor procedures across contexts (K–12 and postsecondary). Intended to guide drafting and implementation of grievance policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on evidence of complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct (§106.45(b)(7)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: General prohibition on questioning about or considering evidence regarding a complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct in Title IX grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to the entirety of a recipient's Title IX grievance procedures for complaints of sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment; aligns with rape-shield protections used in Federal litigation; justified by sensitivity, potential prejudice, and chilling effects; Department is not aware of conflicting rape-shield laws. No standard of relevance should be applied to override this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to rape-shield prohibition (two narrow exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two limited exceptions allow evidence of complainant's prior sexual conduct: (1) to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct, and (2) to prove consent when the evidence concerns specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions mirror the 2020 amendments; parties may assert applicability of exceptions as part of their opportunity to respond; determinations are fact-specific. The Department declined to create broader exceptions such as for exculpatory evidence allowed in criminal trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on impermissible evidence (§106.8(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and others responsible for implementing grievance procedures must be trained on the types of evidence that are impermissible regardless of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required training is intended to help elementary and secondary schools apply the rape-shield prohibition and other evidence exclusions appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent sexual history not subject to complainant-specific rape-shield protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to extend §106.45(b)(7)(iii)'s protections to respondents; respondents' prior sexual conduct is governed by the general relevance standard (§106.2) and assessed case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: complainants require special protections due to historical and societal misperceptions; respondents do not require a special provision. Note situations with counterclaims where a party may be both complainant and respondent — the recipient must apply rape-shield protections to any party designated as a 'complainant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern evidence governed by relevance, not special provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of a respondent's prior sex-based conduct offered as 'pattern' evidence is not given special treatment under §106.45(b)(7)(iii) and must meet the relevance standard in §106.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes pattern evidence may be admissible in other proceedings (e.g., courts) but in Title IX proceedings recipients must objectively evaluate pattern evidence for relevance to the allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern witnesses not covered by rape-shield protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections in §106.45(b)(7)(iii) are not extended to pattern witnesses (witnesses allegedly sexually harassed or assaulted by the same respondent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure fair proceedings with broad admissible evidence, the provision is limited to complainants' sexual interests/prior sexual conduct. Witnesses may still decline to answer particular questions during grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'prior' sexual conduct timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Prior’ sexual conduct refers to any conduct prior to the conclusion of the grievance procedures, not limited to conduct that occurred before the alleged incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with the Department's prior reasoning that evidence offered to prove other sexual behavior should generally be prohibited; 'prior' is used rather than 'other' because it is more widely understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior consensual sexual conduct does not 'by itself' demonstrate consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact of prior consensual sexual conduct between the parties does not 'by itself' demonstrate or imply the complainant's consent to the alleged sex-based harassment or preclude a determination that sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even similarities in types of consent-related communication do not on their own demonstrate consent. The regulation text was revised to add 'by itself' to resolve perceived inconsistencies about proof of consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence about relationships not covered unless directly linked to sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence about a relationship between the parties that is not related to the complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct is not excluded by §106.45(b)(7)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, evidence directly linked to prior sexual conduct (e.g., pregnancy, use of birth control, STI history) is prohibited unless it falls within an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology preference: 'sexual interests or prior sexual conduct'
rubrics_metrics.description: Department maintains the phrase 'sexual interests or prior sexual conduct' rather than alternatives like 'sexual predisposition' or 'prior sexual history/behavior.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: consistent regulatory use of 'conduct' and avoidance of outdated/inflammatory terms like 'predisposition.' Evidence related to sexual interests includes but is not limited to mode of dress, speech, and lifestyle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to use certain procedures for some complaints (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may adopt grievance procedures that apply to some, but not all, complaints of sex discrimination, provided it informs its education community in advance of when those procedures apply and articulates consistent principles in its written grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of factors to articulate include types of sex-based harassment, student-to-student complaints, types of evidence, ages or education levels. Recipient must identify principles explaining when certain procedures will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment when choosing procedures (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether to apply certain procedures to some complaints, the recipient's determination must be made in a manner that treats complainants and respondents equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when varying procedures across complaint types, the requirement of equitable treatment remains; this is a compass constraint on recipients' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using different procedures for different parties in same complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not use different procedures for different parties within the same complaint investigation (e.g., live hearing for one party but not the other), absent a party's need for a disability-related accommodation or language access services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consistent treatment within the same matter unless accommodation needs justify differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of notice of allegations — upon initiation of grievance procedures (§106.45(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the notice of allegations 'upon initiation of the recipient's grievance procedures' (distinct from 'upon receipt of a formal complaint').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows time to review the complaint, consider dismissal threshold issues, confirm accuracy of information, and address safety concerns; but notice must be provided as soon as threshold issues are resolved to ensure prompt and equitable resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of allegations — baseline elements (§106.45(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must include the identities of the parties involved, the conduct alleged to constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or the part, and the date(s) and location(s) of the alleged incident(s), if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may provide additional information but is not required to; information included must be sufficient to allow parties to respond. The Department declined to narrow or broaden the 'conduct alleged' requirement because facts and institutional policies vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must state parties' equal opportunity to access evidence (§106.45(c)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must include a statement that parties are entitled to an equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description of this evidence, and if a description is provided, parties may request and must receive access to the underlying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised to ensure clarity and consistency with evidence-access provisions (§106.45(f)(4)); this helps ensure parties can meaningfully respond to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for written vs oral notice (K–12 vs postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may provide written notice (encouraged for serious conduct) or a simplified/oral notice in appropriate contexts, particularly for elementary and secondary schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice promotes predictability and transparency, but mandatory written notice may impede prompt, developmentally appropriate responses in K–12. Oral notice must still be documented under recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous notice not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide notice to the parties who are known, but simultaneous notice to all parties is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment (§106.45(b)(1)) is required, but simultaneous communication may be impractical or inappropriate; recipients should act consistent with equity when timing differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must precede informal resolution offer
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide the notice of allegations upon initiation of grievance procedures, which necessarily precedes offering parties any opportunity for informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties need notice to make an informed decision about whether to participate in informal resolution. Disclosure exceptions (e.g., §106.44(j)) allow such disclosures when made to carry out the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline sufficiency standard for notice information
rubrics_metrics.description: The information included in the notice must be sufficient to allow the parties to respond to the allegations; recipients have discretion about how detailed the notice is depending on context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A streamlined notice is easier to implement and understand, especially in K–12; additional detail may be provided in cases with more serious conduct or due process concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement includes notice of allegations (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to maintain records documenting their response to complaints of sex discrimination, which includes documentation of the notice of allegations (including orally-provided notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures an audit trail for enforcement and supports due process; recipients should reduce notices to writing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal approach (§106.45(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule adopts a permissive dismissal framework allowing recipients discretion to dismiss complaints in certain circumstances rather than mandating dismissal based on initial threshold determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: mandatory dismissal in 2020 could cause premature/inappropriate dismissals; permissive dismissals better support Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate by allowing investigation when it is unclear initially whether conduct meets the definition of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for dismissal: conduct not under recipient's education program or activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint because the alleged conduct did not occur under the recipient's education program or activity (i.e., outside Title IX coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education program or activity includes but is not limited to conduct in buildings owned/controlled by recognized student organizations and conduct subject to the recipient's disciplinary authority; the recipient has obligation to address sex-based hostile environment even if some conduct occurred outside the program/activity, but Title IX does not apply to conduct wholly outside it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion in terminology and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion in how they label and communicate their processes (e.g., whether to use the term 'dismissal') as long as they effectively convey the circumstances under which a recipient may decline to initiate or continue a Title IX investigation and otherwise comply with §106.45(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using regulatory terminology may aid comparability and enforcement, but age, maturity, and educational level of the student population can justify different language for clarity and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of conflicting State or local law
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(7)(iii) has preemptive effect over conflicting State or local laws to the extent of an actual conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may continue to comply with State law to the extent it does not conflict with these final regulations; in actual conflict, the federal regulation controls.
